messages:
amal: FYI I ran the paged-attn perf microbench after the heapmap shard-indexing patch landed. Seeing a regression on long sequences (>=1024). p50 token latency up ~33%. Anyone free to help bisect? @jordan @kai

jordan: On it. Which commit range are we looking at? Is this the new heapmap + scatter-alloc change?

amal: Yes — commit 6d9f7c. Repro command I used:
```
./bench/paged_attn_bench --model=gpt2-xl --seq=1024 --batch=4 --iters=200
```
Baseline (before) p50 ~12ms, current p50 ~16ms. GPU SM util dropped 89% -> 74%. memory bandwidth up ~12%.

kai: That smells like extra pointer-chasing in the block lookup path. Heapmap introduced an indirection per page lookup. Do we have a flamegraph or hotspot list? @perf-bot can you paste the last trace?

perf-bot: perf run summary attached to CI run paged-attn/heapmap-indirect-A:
- paged_kv::lookup 41%
- gather_kernel 18%
- attention_fwd (fused) 14%
- memcpy (async compaction) 9%

rachel: Also observed higher fragmentation in the free-list after the new allocator: a lot more small chunks and higher free-chunk churn. That could increase compaction frequency and cause extra memcpy overhead.

jordan: Quick local experiment: toggling a fallback to contiguous-shard (pre-heapmap layout) reverts numbers back close to baseline. So allocation layout seems to be the primary hit.

amal: I compiled a quick toggle patch: `heapmap->use_indirect = false` and ran the same bench. Results: p50 -> 12.5ms. So indirection is the culprit in practice.

kai: Hypothesis: the extra indirection prevents contiguous page pointer layout, killing L2 prefetch and causing scattered loads in the gather kernel. That increases latency even though aggregate throughput (bandwidth) goes up. Possible mitigations:
- change heapmap to store contiguous page pointers per shard (flattened)
- add a tiny inline cache (per-request / per-thread) for last N page pointers to remove repeated chasing
- prefer kernel variants that tolerate scatter (FlashAttention v2 fallback) when frag_ratio high

jordan: We prototyped an 8-entry inline LRU for page pointers in-thread; microbench shows ~30% reduction in lookup cost and ~10% overall p50 improvement for seq=1024. Memory overhead negligible. Need to test at scale.

rachel: I'll add telemetry counters to the runtime: frag_ratio, avg_indirection_depth, inline_cache_hits, compaction_count. We should gate batching decisions on frag_ratio.

amal: Action items:
1) jordan - run git-bisect across the 6b..6d range and confirm the exact diff that introduced the perf regression
2) kai - prototype the inline pointer cache and test on CI microbenches
3) rachel - add telemetry for frag_ratio / indirection metrics and add an alert if p50 regresses >20% on staging
4) amal - open a short-term rollback of the shard-indexing change on staging to stop customer regressions

perf-bot: CI job queued: `paged-attn/heapmap-indirect-A/B` and `paged-attn/inline-cache-proto`. ETA ~30m for first numbers.

jordan: Also note kernel-selection strategy: fused attention microbenchmarks indicate fused-v3 loses to FlashAttention-linearized when page-pointer indirection is high. We should prefer FlashAttention-linearized for high-frag cases in the routing table.

kai: Small note on batching heuristics: current packing mixes long and short sequences which increases random-access ratio for KV. Switching to seq-aware packing (pairing similar length sequences) reduced random lookups and gave ~8% p50 improvement in a local run. Might be quick win.

amal: Thanks everyone. I'll file an RFC summarizing hypotheses + benched numbers and include the perf traces. For immediate mitigation I'm rolling back 6d on staging and adding a temporary fallback to contiguous-shard when frag_ratio > 0.35. Reassign if you find any surprises in the bisect/CI runs.

jordan: ping when CI numbers land, I'll review the bisect results.

kai: I'll push the inline-cache draft later today and link bench scripts.

(End of thread)
